versions.changelog: SKILL.md now says where the complete project lives: the GitHub repository is the full, unabridged version (identical core plus the optional openclaw/ host integration), while this registry package is deliberately slimmed to the auditable core.

Benefit-first documentation: SKILL.md/README/说明.md now open with what the skill does for you (nothing forgotten, the goal never gets lost, knows when and how to recall) plus a before/after table; fixed a broken heading fragment that rendered as a stray line; the package boundary is now explicit (registry = audited portable core, GitHub = complete project).

Published docs now describe only the published package: permissions list file read/write and environment only (no shell/subprocess/PowerShell), and all localised sections are compact, consistent summaries of the portable core.

Narrow purge scope (artifact filename + read-only identity + lstat re-check) and exclusive archive creation (O_CREAT|O_EXCL; collision aborts with exit 10). Adds per-directory archive_id and metadata app/format validation.

Fixes append-target selection: --append now requires the complete artifact filename and verifies archive_metadata read-only before writing; ambiguous or foreign targets abort with exit 9. Adds --db-path for explicit selection.

Documentation accuracy: one consistent retention policy everywhere (30 days default, 1..3650, unlimited only by explicit flag), no capability claims for code outside the package, README/说明 rewritten with quick start, disclosure table, FAQ and issue links.

Packaging boundary: the artifact is now exactly the portable Python core (no JS/PowerShell); openclaw/ stays in the repo with its own manifest. Also removes PATH-based Python resolution in the legacy cleanup script.
Bounded retention (30 days by default), INFINITY_CONTEXT_NO_ARCHIVE=1 off switch, --purge-only manual retention pass, consolidated install docs, attribution line.

Blast-radius containment + capability disclosure. T09: cleanup.py now requires the owner-only .infinity-context-archive marker (written by the archiver), refuses protected directories, deletes only full-filename allowlist artifacts, never recurses, schema-gates VACUUM, re-checks each candidate with lstat before unlink, and needs --apply --confirm-destructive; --init-marker migrates old archives. Tp4: SKILL.md/README.md open with a Security & Privacy Disclosure table naming persist/delete/in-place-rewrite/fallback, SKILL.md adds a first-run consent requirement, and the description names the cleanup and redaction tools.

Fail-closed output directory. A non-ASCII --output-dir is now refused (status error, exit 8) before anything is created, instead of silently moving the archive to ~/.openclaw/sqlite-data with only a stderr warning. Passing --allow-dir-fallback restores the fallback, which is still reported in the JSON result (archive_dir_fallback, requested_dir, archive_dir) and warned about on stderr.

Reviewer-driven hardening. T09-1: all four ingestion limits are validated to 1..hard ceiling in the CLI and in read_messages(), so a negative byte limit can no longer reach file.read(-1) and an oversized value can no longer exceed the documented cap. T09-2: secure_fs now checks every existing path component (not just the parent) with islink and compares each component with its resolved path, which also catches Windows directory junctions.

Author-requested signature refresh: the attribution line at the end of README.md and the Chinese README now credits deepseek-v4-flash/pro without the stray separator and adds Gemini3.8-flash. Source-install comments pin v1.6.4 with the matching version guard.

Every language section of README.md now carries the same security and privacy disclosure as English (local-only, full trajectory export before compaction, redacted local SQLite/FTS5 archive, fail-closed backup destruction, owner-only ACL with 30-day retention, opt-in auto-wake, integrity check). Source-install comments pin v1.6.3 with a matching version guard.

T08: every source-install quick-start now pins the reviewed tag (v1.6.2) and a version guard stops the install when the checked-out SKILL.md version differs from the tag. T09: ingestion is bounded while reading - at most --max-session-bytes (64 MiB) from the transcript head, a line over --max-line-bytes (1 MiB) is dropped before JSON or regex, and parsing stops at --max-messages / --max-total-chars; the result reports ingest.truncated and ingest.truncated_reason. In-place redaction refuses a file over 64 MiB before reading it.

v1.6.1 path-resolution fix. ClawHub's 1.6.0 review found a precise remaining flaw: the redaction helper could rewrite user-writable files outside the declared directory through symlinked ancestors. redact_file_in_place now resolves every symbolic link before deciding scope: the lexical path must be inside --allow-dir, the realpath-resolved target must be inside the resolved allowed directory, and the lexical relative path must equal the resolved relative path, which rejects a junction such as allowed/jump/x. The regression suite creates a real directory junction and proves the outside file is refused and left untouched. Verified: 3 rounds, 308 checks, 0 failures.

v1.6.0 scope-and-transparency release, addressing the two concerns raised in the 1.5.0 ClawHub review: 'under-scoped file mutation' and 'can silently store sensitive archives in an unexpected location'. In-place redaction now refuses to run without --allow-dir (exit 7), so the engine can never modify a file outside a caller-declared directory; the OpenClaw integration already passes the backup root. A non-ASCII output path that would break SQLite still falls back to an ASCII directory, but the run now prints SECURITY_WARN: ARCHIVE_DIR_FALLBACK and the JSON result carries archive_dir, requested_dir and archive_dir_fallback, so the effective location is never changed silently. Regression tests cover both behaviours. Verified: 3 rounds, 305 checks, 0 failures.

v1.5.0 fail-closed redaction. The audit found silent failure branches in the redaction path itself. Rule loading no longer swallows exceptions: malformed JSON, a non-object schema, a non-list custom_redact_rules, a non-dict entry, an empty pattern or a non-string replace raises RedactionConfigError and exits 2 before any file or database is created. All built-in and custom regexes are precompiled at startup and an uncompilable pattern aborts; redact_sensitive_info no longer catches re.error and continues. session_key is sanitised before any path or filename is built - values outside the safe identifier set, or that themselves look sensitive, become opaque-<sha256[:16]> and never reach a filename, the table or the FTS index. The transcript is fully redacted in memory and then written in a single transaction; on failure the transaction rolls back, the handle is closed first, and only a database created by that run is deleted, so an existing archive being appended to is never removed. New regression suite covers every branch. Verified: 3 rounds, 0 failures.

v1.4.0 fail-closed hardening + mandatory attribution. T09-1: secure_fs no longer returns a best-effort success - it re-reads the POSIX mode with lstat (mode + owner) and raises UnsafeArchiveError when owner-only access cannot be enforced, and the Windows DACL path raises on any failure. session_to_sqlite.py reacts by closing the SQLite handle first, destroying the half-written database and its -wal/-shm sidecars, and exiting with code 3; --allow-insecure-storage is the only opt-out and is reported as insecure_storage:true. Symbolic links on the target path are refused and a newly created archive directory is removed again if it cannot be secured. T09-2: redact_file_in_place no longer writes to a predictable '<name>.redact.tmp' - it uses tempfile.mkstemp (O_EXCL, 0600), refuses symlink targets and foreign-owned parents, fsyncs before the atomic replace, always removes the temp file, and re-secures the final file; the integration passes --allow-dir so paths outside the backup root are refused. LICENSE: MIT with a mandatory attribution clause - any use, including modified variants, must credit Pondsi. Verified: 3 rounds, 262 checks, 0 failures.

v1.3.3 robustness fix found while validating the published package end to end: a JSONL transcript beginning with a UTF-8 byte-order mark made json.loads fail on the first line, and the archiver skipped it silently, so a single-line transcript produced zero chunks. Both the transcript reader and the in-place redactor now open files as utf-8-sig, which consumes a BOM and behaves like utf-8 otherwise. Verified both ways - a BOM file and a plain file each archive exactly one chunk. Verified: 3 rounds, 237 checks, 0 failures.

v1.3.2 documentation correctness. Fixed two defects in the 1.3.1 instructions that would have broken the out-of-the-box promise: (1) the registry slug was written as infinity-context, but the published slug is infinitycontext, so the install command returned 'Skill not found' - every quick-start in every language now uses the real slug and shows a concrete command for dsh/Claude Code and for OpenClaw; (2) the dsh discovery rules were wrong - the official DeepSeek Harness documentation and dsh-skill-filesystem state that a skill is a directory bundle one level deep or a flat file, nested SKILL.md is deliberately not discovered, name/description are required and name must be kebab-case, and the folder name is not part of the identity. Verified: 3 rounds, 236 checks, 0 failures.

v1.3.1 security hardening. T09: the archive directory, database and WAL sidecars are now owner-only - 0700/0600 on POSIX and a protected DACL (current user + LOCAL SYSTEM) on Windows, written with in-process Win32 API calls instead of spawning icacls; database files are created atomically with 0600 so no file ever exists with wider permissions; a foreign-owned archive directory is refused. T08: every quick-start is registry-first and pins the audited tag v1.3.1 plus checksums.txt verification; cp -r was replaced by explicit per-file copies in all languages. Added scripts/secure_fs.py, root checksums.txt and .gitattributes; SKILL.md trimmed with other languages in references/languages.md. DeepSeek Harness (dsh) and OpenClaw are both documented as out-of-the-box hosts. Verified: 3 rounds, 0 failures.

v1.3.0 Structural release: the portable Python core and the OpenClaw/Windows integration are now separate, so audit findings T07 (tool hijacking) and T08 (insecure dependencies) cannot recur by construction. The published package contains no JavaScript, no PowerShell and no install-time fetch - the audited artifact is exactly what runs. T07: every external command in the integration resolves to an absolute path from System32 or a known install directory, PATH lookups removed, process PATH narrowed, zero bare calls. T08: the package is self-contained; the optional integration is documented in openclaw/README.md with a pinned revision, checksums.txt and explicit file-by-file copy. Added portable scripts/cleanup.py and scripts/search.py. DeepSeek Harness (dsh) documented as a first-class host. Verified: 3 rounds, 0 failures.

v1.2.1 Registry compliance: the published package ships no .js files because ClawHub static analysis rejects child_process (suspicious.dangerous_exec) with no suppression mechanism. The optional OpenClaw compaction hook (src/handler.js, src/HOOK.md, src/integrity.json) is distributed in the GitHub repository only and is documented as such in README/SKILL/说明. Everything in this package runs as scripts the agent invokes through its declared tools. Retains all v1.2.0 hardening: fail-closed redaction, declared opt-in auto-recovery, hook integrity manifest, absolute executable paths, cross-host positioning (DeepSeek Harness dsh first-class), EXIF-stripped sponsor images. Verified 3 rounds / 192 checks / 0 failures.

v1.2.0 Security & compliance hardening (external audit round 2). Fail-closed redaction: backup is destroyed and aborted if the redactor is unavailable/fails - no plaintext retention (opt-in only). Removed the external notification process so behaviour matches the documented log-only policy. Auto-recovery is now a declared opt-in capability (enableAutoWake), single validated attempt per round, audited with WAKE_REQUEST, no hidden retry loop. Hook integrity: handler.js verifies pipeline.ps1 against integrity.json (SHA-256), rejects symlinks/empty files, requires the script marker, launches PowerShell from its absolute System32 path; pipeline.ps1 calls the Python engine directly. Cross-host positioning: standard Agent Skills skill with first-class DeepSeek Harness (dsh) support; OpenClaw documented as optional; frontmatter declares license/compatibility/metadata. Sponsor QR images had EXIF stripped losslessly. Verified: 3 rounds / 192 checks / 0 failures incl. a real end-to-end export.

v1.1.0 Privacy & Compliance hardening: removed cmd.exe shell invocation (direct CLI + argument validation), trajectory backups now ACL-restricted + redacted + 30-day retention, redaction applied before metadata derivation with expanded rules (JWT/AWS/PEM/connection strings/PII), data minimization via MAX_ARCHIVE_LENGTH truncation, declared allowed-tools scope, privacy notice. Verified: 3 rounds + self-audit = 171 checks, 0 failures.

v1.0.0 security hardening: T05 deny-by-default agent allowlist (fail-closed, no agents-directory enumeration), T09 cleanup script hardening (range validation, canonical path anchoring, extension allowlist, symlink skip, -WhatIf). Verified with 3 rounds (117 checks).

InfinityContext 0.1.7 — Security Model Update

- Hardened all privileged operations with a strict "deny by default" security model.
- Allowlist for agent operations is now fail-closed: no fallback to allow-all if the allowlist is empty.
- Scripts no longer enumerate all agents; only explicitly allowed agents are processed.
- `cleanup-old-backups.ps1` now enforces canonical path checks, valid extensions, and supports audit with `-WhatIf`/`-Confirm`.
- Updated documentation and removed the outdated skill-card.md file.

InfinityContext v0.1.6 brings improved integration and deployment workflow.

- Scripts reorganized: `pipeline.ps1` now must be placed next to the hook for correct execution.
- Installation instructions updated to clarify script placement and task scheduling.
- Now leverages OpenClaw’s native event hooks; standalone system scheduled tasks are optional.
- Sponsorship options added (Alipay and WeChat).
- Documentation updated in multiple languages.
- Deprecated `skill-card.md` removed.

- Added cleanup-old-backups.ps1 script for scheduled backup maintenance.
- Introduced session_to_sqlite.py for direct Python-based session conversion to SQLite.
- Updated PowerShell scripts (main-session-monitor.ps1, pipeline.ps1, session-to-sqlite.ps1) for improved backup, pipeline, and session handling.
- Enhanced src/handler.js and replaced/updated src/session_to_sqlite.py for streamlined integration with the new backup and compaction process.
- Improves automation and reliability of memory optimization and session management pipelines.

InfinityContext 0.1.4

- Updated SKILL.md documentation, including corrected scheduled task PowerShell commands (removed the -WindowStyle Hidden parameter).
- No code or logic changes; update is documentation-only.

- Broadened description: InfinityContext is now described as a universal context compression and memory optimization solution for any AI agent platform, not just OpenClaw.
- Documentation updated to reflect compatibility with Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Dify, Ollama, and more—not limited to a single agent environment.
- No code or implementation changes—documentation (README.md, SKILL.md, SPONSORS.md) only.

- Updated SKILL.md scheduled task examples to use direct PowerShell calls (removed reliance on wscript/RunHidden.vbs).
- No other significant code or documentation changes detected.

## InfinityContext 0.2.0 Changelog

- Added explicit `version: 0.2.0` field to SKILL.md.
- No functional or implementation changes; documentation update only.
- All instructions, configurations, and descriptions remain the same other than version metadata.

Initial release of InfinityContext: multi-layer context compression and memory optimization for OpenClaw.

- Prevents small model context overflow with configurable recent token retention and watchdog triggers.
- Adds a compaction pipeline: automatic session backup, SQLite storage with FTS5 search, and streamlined MEMORY.md.
- Integrates a compaction-pipeline hook to intercept manual, automatic, and watchdog compaction events.
- Supports deduplicated backups and robust failure handling.
- Provides multi-language documentation and setup instructions.
